children: This week’s roundup brought a mixed set of transportation stories, with electric-vehicle makers facing uneven demand, production pressure and differing results across international markets.
Tesla Inc.
remained central to the conversation, while rivals
Polestar Automotive Holding UK Limited
and
Lucid Group Inc.
offered contrasting updates on sales and manufacturing.
Outside the EV sector,
Delta Air Lines Inc.
revisited plans for a new Saudi Arabia route after deadly attacks at Riyadh’s international airport.
Polestar’s International Sales Lose Momentum

Polestar shares traded lower Thursday after the automaker reported weaker third-quarter retail sales when its U.S. business was excluded from the calculation. The company estimated third-quarter 2026 retail sales at 14,371 vehicles, representing a 1% increase from the same period a year earlier. Through the first nine months, estimated retail sales reached 44,790 cars. That nine-month figure was up 0.6% compared with the prior-year period, indicating only modest growth as the company continues navigating demand across global markets outside the United States.
Cybertruck Ambitions Meet Tougher Math
Elon Musk

set ambitious expectations for the Cybertruck, the electric pickup launched by Tesla in 2023. Three years later, new figures suggest the vehicle remains far below those targets. Musk had envisioned a significantly larger annual sales outcome for the Cybertruck, but demand has not matched the scale of those plans. The latest calculations point to a substantial gap between the goal and the number of vehicles sold. The Cybertruck’s performance adds another layer to the discussion surrounding Tesla’s vehicle demand, even as the company’s stock remained steady during Thursday’s trading session.

children: Tesla Sees a Slow Start In India

Tesla reported 486,532 deliveries during the third quarter, exceeding analyst expectations. However, fewer than 1,000 of those vehicles were delivered in India during the period. India has therefore contributed only a small portion of Tesla’s global delivery total during the first 12 months of operations there. Still, early signs suggest the market may be beginning to develop momentum. The contrast between limited current sales and improving market interest gives investors a reason to watch India’s next phase, particularly as Tesla works to establish a broader presence in the country.
Delta Reviews Riyadh Service After Attacks
Delta is reconsidering its planned Oct. 23 introduction of daily flights between Atlanta and Riyadh following deadly attacks at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. Delta CEO
Ed Bastian

said in a CNBC interview Friday that the airline was disappointed by the developments. The company is assessing whether the route should begin as scheduled. "Safety is going to make the call," Bastian said. Delta plans to notify customers of its decision soon, leaving the new service’s launch dependent on the airline’s review.
Lucid Trims Production as Deliveries Miss Forecasts

Lucid reduced its production output while working to move inventory after third-quarter deliveries fell short of analyst expectations. The automaker produced 2,954 vehicles and delivered 3,806 vehicles during the third quarter of 2026. Analysts had expected 3,709 vehicles to be produced and 4,687 delivered. Production declined 38% from the prior quarter, when Lucid manufactured 4,774 vehicles. The reduction came as the company confronted an inventory buildup alongside softer-than-expected deliveries.
